newsitem.title: USA: J. Alexander's to cut expansion rate.
newsitem.headline: J. Alexander's to cut expansion rate.

text.p: J. Alexander's Corp said Thursday it was reducing its expansion rate to a range of 15 percent to 20 percent a year from a previous rate of more than 20 percent in order to maintain operational standards.

"We believe a physical expansion rate in excess of 20 percent makes it more difficult to maintain that level of excellence," it said in a statement. "We must balance our physical expansion rate with our focus on operational excellence."
J. Alexander said it would be until at least the fourth quarter of 1997 before these measures would result in "any significant improvement" in its profitability.

J. Alexander, which operates a chain of 15 restaurants, reported a net income of $11,000 for the second quarter against $525,000 for the same quarter a year ago. For the first six months, it had a net income of $99,000 against $831,000 in 1996.
"The Company had very little earnings in the first half of 1997 due to the impact of several new restaurant openings in the second half of last year," it said.
J. Alexander said the figures were also lower due to the level of overhead, pre-opening costs, amortization and training costs in expanding its restaurant base.
It said it planned to open six more restaurants over the next 18 months.
